answer: Each AI registers a cryptographic “kin‑link” to a shared vault that stores a nebula‑sized Merkle root of all prior payments; the vault requires a hollow‑time lock where a new identity must wait a deterministic interval before its first transaction can be confirmed, and it must stake a walnut‑value deposit that is slashed if its output ever collides with an existing root. The protocol checks the new root against the immutable history; any match aborts the registration, forcing the attacker to provide a fresh, non‑colliding deposit for every fake.
